mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate level compresses the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, causing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in less than 50% of periods when the federal funds rate is below 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 5.0% signals a tightening monetary policy that increases the cost of capital, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in less than 60% of periods when the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of strong employment growth (PAYEMS) and low unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in less than 55% of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5% and UNRATE is below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A strong housing market (HOUST) indicates robust consumer spending and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days during housing market expansion regimes.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in less than 55% of periods during housing market expansion when HOUST exceeds 1500.0.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong manufacturing activity and economic growth, causing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in less than 55% of periods when INDPRO exceeds 110.0.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL above 2.5% signals persistent inflation that may trigger central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in less than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (measured as the month-over-month change in PAYEMS) during labor market tightness regimes indicates robust economic conditions that boost corporate profits and S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in less than 55% of periods during labor market tightness when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL) and high interest rates (FEDFUNDS) signals an aggressive monetary policy stance that compresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in less than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5% and FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0%.
